sentences.text: This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the 1st accused in Crime No.299 of 2025 of Iritty Police Station, Kannur, registered for the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n)(f) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3.

According to the prosecution, the 1 st accused had repeatedly raped the de facto complainant from July 2017 to January, 2025 and also committed criminal breach of trust of 9.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments and Rs.4.8 Lakhs and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard Sri.Ramees P.K., the learned Counsel for the petitioner as well as Sri.Noushad K.A., the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.

The learned Counsel for the petitioner contended that 2025:KER:39251 the prosecution allegations are totally false and the entire allegations have been concocted for the purpose of compelling the brother of the petitioner to withdraw certain criminal cases filed by him against the siblings of the de facto complainant.

It was also submitted that the nature of allegations raised is impossible of belief and that even if the same are assumed to be true, it can only reveal a consensual relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant.

The learned Counsel further contended that petitioner had no connection with the de facto complainant from January, 2018 till date and that he is employed in UAE and also that he is willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed by this Court.

6. The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the allegations are serious and considering the nature of acts alleged by the de facto complainant as also the allegation that the petitioner had raped the de facto complainant in 2017 and his friends are alleged to have outraged her modesty by making unwelcome gestures and comments in 2025, custodial interrogation is necessary.
To appreciate the arguments of the respective Counsel, this Court called for the case diary.

On a perusal of the case diary and on appreciation of the investigation conducted so far, it is noticed that the alleged rape is stated to have taken place in July, 2017 at the house of the de facto complainant.

sentences.text: On 01.07.2017 and 10.07.2017 petitioner is alleged to have raped the de facto complainant and allegedly took her photographs on his mobile phone.
Subsequently, 9.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments, 2 gold bangles and a further amount of Rs.4.8 Lakhs were taken by him from her after allegedly threatening to show the photographs to others.
An additional statement is also given by the victim alleging that the friends of the petitioner had been asking her for sexual favours referring to the rape committed by the petitioner.
8. The statement of the de facto complainant reveals that, though the incident of rape is alleged to have taken place in the year 2017, she had not divulged the same to any person until 2025.
Petitioner is stated to be employed in UAE and came down to India to attend to his wife, who is alleged to be critically ill.
It was at this juncture that the FIR was lodged.

The circumstances pointed 2025:KER:39251 out by the petitioner also indicate that there are criminal cases between the petitioner's brother and the de facto complainant's siblings, which is registered as Crime No.51 of 2018 of Iritty Police Station.
The said case is stated to be posted for trial.
From 2018 till 2025, when there were apparently criminal cases existing between the siblings of the de facto complainant and the brother of the petitioner, no complaint was filed.
The nature of allegations prima facie indicates a possible consensual relationship between the two grown ups.

9. Having regard to the entire circumstances mentioned above, this Court is of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not necessary, though for the purpose of recovery of the alleged mobile phone and gold ornaments, limited custody is to be granted.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 17.06.2025, 18.06.2025 & 19.06.2025 from 10 a.m to 5 p.m and shall subject himself to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner, then, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence or contact the victim or her family members;
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
(f) Petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction.
